title: One-Shot any Code
abstract: We first provide a simple proof showing that any single-shot code is self-correcting. We then show that any $[[n,k]]$ CSS quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) code can be transformed into an $[[nm,k]]$ CSS QLDPC code with single-shot (SS) quantum error correction and an efficient local decoder which runs in $O(\log m)$ parallel time. Below a constant threshold $p_{\rm RG}>0$ for joint local stochastic physical and measurement noise, the logical failure probability over $T$ correction rounds is bounded by \begin{equation*}   O(T n)\exp[-Ω(m^α)] \end{equation*} for a constant $α>0$; we say that the \textit{threshold} is $p_{\rm RG}$ and \textit{error suppression} is $Ω(m^α)$. Moreover, if the input code is equipped with a single-shot decoder with threshold $p_c>0$ and error suppression $Ω(n^β)$, then the output code \textit{enhances} the error suppression to $Ω(m^α n^β)$, while maintaining the decoder-independent threshold $p_{\rm RG}$, and thus \textit{enhanced} if $p_c < p_{\rm RG}$.
summary: This paper develops a method to upgrade any quantum error-correcting code to support single-shot (SS) syndrome measurements, a significant advance over traditional time-consuming syndrome extraction. By constructing an output code $	ext{[[nm, k]]}$ from an input code $	ext{[[n, k]]}$ using an efficient RG decoder, the authors demonstrate robust error suppression over many correction rounds. This breakthrough addresses the temporal bottleneck in fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The goal is to equip an arbitrary Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) code with single-shot (SS) quantum error correction while maintaining bounded check weight and qubit degree.
main_result: The authors show that any single-shot stabilizer code is self-correcting and provide a method to transform any input code into an output code with SS QEC, achieving error suppression $\Omega(m^\alpha n^ eta)$.
method: The core method involves constructing an output code $	ext{[[nm, k]]}$ from an input $	ext{[[n, k]]}$ code using a renormalization-group (RG) decoder that runs efficiently in $O(\log m)$ parallel time.
model_or_system: The work analyzes Quantum Error Correction (QEC) using CSS QLDPC codes. The focus is on moving from conventional syndrome extraction (which requires multiple time steps) to single-shot syndrome measurements, controlling both physical and measurement noise.
key_observables: Logical failure probability over $T$ rounds, error suppression $\Omega(m^\alpha)$, and the threshold $p_{	ext{RG}}$.
important_parameters: The noise threshold $p_{	ext{RG}} > 0$, the error suppression exponent $\alpha > 0$, and the input/output code parameters $(n, k)$ and $(nm, k)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes local stochastic (LS) rates for physical errors and measurement errors, and the construction does not require the code to have a three-dimensional geometric realization.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the self-correcting nature of single-shot codes, proves the general transformation from any QLDPC code to an SS-correcting code, and analyzes the resulting error suppression bounds over multiple correction rounds.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general framework for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation by upgrading existing quantum codes to support single-shot syndrome measurements, which is crucial for scaling quantum memory and computation.
